patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of persistent fatigue and several episodes of lower abdominal pain. Despite being on sick leave for 2 weeks, symptoms have not improved. She expresses a concern that she might have cancer and requests a diagnostic laparoscopy. She was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months prior, currently taking omeprazole.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Works as a nurse, has been under a lot of stress at work.

Review_of_Systems.Skin: Numerous crusts along the left arm veins
Review_of_Systems.Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur along the right-upper sternal border
Review_of_Systems.Musculoskeletal: Generalized weakness of the proximal muscles

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with fatigue, episodes of lower abdominal pain, and a self-stated high cancer concern.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on? Patient: I’m a 26-year-old nurse, and for about two months I’ve had persistent fatigue and I’ve been looking paler than usual. I also had a few episodes of lower abdominal pain, and despite being on sick leave for two weeks I haven’t felt any better. I’m very stressed and worried it could be something serious like cancer, so I’m requesting further evaluation.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any joint swelling, but I do feel generalized weakness in my muscles and I’ve been feeling quite tired and depressed.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on my scalp. My main issues are persistent fatigue and generalized muscle weakness, with a few episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a sensation of itchiness lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any itching or an itchiness sensation. It’s mainly the persistent fatigue, feeling paler, generalized weakness, and those few episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble raising your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “I can raise my arms above my head, but I feel weaker than I used to and it seems harder to keep up strength for longer periods.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any loss of vision or any vision changes without pain. It’s mostly the persistent fatigue, feeling paler, generalized proximal muscle weakness, and a few episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s been so high it feels like you’re burning up—something above 104°F (40°C) that makes you feel extremely hot or dizzy?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any fever like that—nothing above 104°F. I’ve mainly been feeling persistently exhausted, paler than usual, and weak in my proximal muscles, along with those occasional episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, I’ve been unusually stressed and overwhelmed at work, and I think it’s been worsening my exhaustion. I’m also worried about what it could be, especially since I haven’t improved even after being off work for two weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate. It’s been mainly persistent fatigue and generalized weakness, with a few episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills or any episodes like that.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breasts, and I haven’t felt anything fixed or not moving. It’s mainly persistent fatigue and paleness, along with generalized proximal muscle weakness and those occasional lower abdominal pain episodes.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: “Yes, I’ve had some discomfort in my lower abdomen, but I haven’t really noticed any specific pain on the sides of my back between my ribs and hips.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed calf pain when I walk that improves with rest—I’ve mainly been dealing with persistent fatigue, feeling paler, and generalized weakness, along with occasional lower abdominal discomfort.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual. It’s mainly the persistent fatigue, paleness, and weakness in my proximal muscles, with those occasional episodes of lower abdominal discomfort.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, I do find it more difficult to keep my strength up when I lift my arms—especially for longer periods, like when I’m reaching or holding things above my head—but I can still lift them.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you often use the same joints repeatedly—like typing, playing an instrument, or doing manual work—and have you noticed any pain or stiffness?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, as a nurse I do a lot of repetitive manual work—typing charts, lifting, and moving patients—so my arms and shoulders get sore and feel more tiring over the day, but I haven’t had specific joint stiffness or swelling.”
